title: Reactions of Metals with Water and Acids
content:
# Reactions of Metals with Water and Acids

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe reactions of metals with water
- Describe reactions of metals with dilute acids
- Write balanced equations for these reactions
- Explain the pattern of reactivity

## Introduction

The reactions of metals with water and acids help us understand and confirm the reactivity series. More reactive metals react more vigorously, producing characteristic observations.

## Key Concepts

### Reactions of Metals with Water

**General equation:**
$$\text{Metal} + \text{Water} \rightarrow \text{Metal hydroxide} + \text{Hydrogen}$$

**Specific examples:**

**Potassium + Water:**
$$\text{2K} + \text{2H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{2KOH} + \text{H}_2$$

*Observations:*
- Melts into a ball and floats
- Moves rapidly across water surface
- Burns with a **lilac flame**
- May explode
- Solution turns alkaline (pH > 7)

**Sodium + Water:**
$$\text{2Na} + \text{2H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{2NaOH} + \text{H}_2$$

*Observations:*
- Melts into a ball and floats
- Fizzes vigorously
- Moves rapidly on water surface
- May catch fire (yellow flame) if held in place
- Solution turns alkaline

**Lithium + Water:**
$$\text{2Li} + \text{2H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{2LiOH} + \text{H}_2$$

*Observations:*
- Floats
- Fizzes steadily (slower than Na)
- Gets smaller and disappears
- Solution turns alkaline

**Calcium + Water:**
$$\text{Ca} + \text{2H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{H}_2$$

*Observations:*
- Sinks (calcium is denser than water)
- Bubbles of hydrogen form
- Goes cloudy (calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble)
- Solution is alkaline

**Magnesium + Water:**
$$\text{Mg} + \text{2H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(OH)}_2 + \text{H}_2$$

*Observations:*
- Very slow reaction with cold water
- Few bubbles form over several days
- Reacts much faster with steam:
$$\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2\text{O(g)} \rightarrow \text{MgO} + \text{H}_2$$

[DIAGRAM: Apparatus for magnesium reacting with steam - showing test tube with magnesium ribbon heated, steam passing over it]

### Reactions with Steam

Metals below calcium in the reactivity series react with steam (not cold water):

| Metal | Equation |
|-------|----------|
| Mg | Mg + H₂O(g) → MgO + H₂ |
| Zn | Zn + H₂O(g) → ZnO + H₂ |
| Fe | 3Fe + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂ |

### Reactions of Metals with Dilute Acids

**General equation:**
$$\text{Metal} + \text{Acid} \rightarrow \text{Salt} + \text{Hydrogen}$$

**With hydrochloric acid (HCl) → chloride salts:**
$$\text{Mg} + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{MgCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Zn} + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Fe} + \text{2HCl} \rightarrow \text{FeCl}_2 + \text{H}_2$$

**With sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄) → sulfate salts:**
$$\text{Mg} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{MgSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{ZnSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$$
$$\text{Fe} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{FeSO}_4 + \text{H}_2$$

### Observations with Dilute Acids

| Metal | Observations with dilute HCl |
|-------|------------------------------|
| Mg | Vigorous fizzing, gets hot, metal disappears quickly |
| Al | Slow at first, then moderate fizzing (oxide layer) |
| Zn | Moderate fizzing, metal dissolves |
| Fe | Slow fizzing, solution turns pale green |
| Cu | No reaction |

### Testing for Hydrogen Gas

**Test:** Apply a burning splint to the gas
**Positive result:** A squeaky pop

[DIAGRAM: Test tube with metal in acid, collecting gas, burning splint test]

### Why Don't Unreactive Metals React?

Copper, silver, and gold are below hydrogen in the reactivity series:
- They cannot displace hydrogen from acids
- They hold onto their electrons too tightly
- No reaction occurs with dilute HCl or H₂SO₄

## Worked Examples

**Example 1:** Write a balanced equation for the reaction of calcium with water.

**Solution:**
- Calcium reacts with water to form calcium hydroxide and hydrogen
- Calcium has a 2+ charge, so formula is Ca(OH)₂
$$\text{Ca} + \text{2H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{H}_2$$

---

**Example 2:** Describe what you would see when magnesium ribbon is added to dilute sulfuric acid.

**Solution:**
- Bubbles/fizzing/effervescence
- The magnesium ribbon gets smaller/dissolves/disappears
- The solution gets warm/hot
- The solution remains colourless

---

**Example 3:** Write a balanced equation for zinc reacting with dilute hydrochloric acid, including state symbols.

**Solution:**
$$\text{Zn(s)} + \text{2HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2\text{(aq)} + \text{H}_2\text{(g)}$$

---

**Example 4:** Explain why copper does not react with dilute sulfuric acid.

**Solution:**
- Copper is below hydrogen in the reactivity series
- Copper is less reactive than hydrogen
- Copper cannot displace hydrogen from the acid
- Therefore no reaction occurs

## Common Mistakes

- **Mistake:** Saying metals react with cold water when they only react with steam
- **Correct:** Only K, Na, Li, Ca react with cold water; others need steam or don't react

- **Mistake:** Forgetting to balance equations properly
- **Correct:** Remember: 2K + 2H₂O (not K + H₂O)

- **Mistake:** Confusing the products - hydroxides from water, salts from acids
- **Correct:** Water → hydroxide + H₂; Acid → salt + H₂

## Practice Questions

1. Write a balanced equation for the reaction of sodium with water. (2 marks)

2. Describe what you would observe when a small piece of potassium is added to water. (4 marks)

3. Write a balanced equation with state symbols for the reaction of magnesium with dilute hydrochloric acid. (2 marks)

4. A student adds iron filings to dilute sulfuric acid.
   a) Write a balanced equation for the reaction. (2 marks)
   b) Describe what the student would observe. (2 marks)
   c) How could the student test for the gas produced? (2 marks)

5. Explain, in terms of the reactivity series, why zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid but copper does not. (3 marks)

6. Compare the reactions of lithium and calcium with water. (4 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Effervescence | The production of bubbles of gas |
| Hydroxide | A compound containing OH⁻ ions |
| Salt | A compound formed when an acid reacts with a metal or base |
| Squeaky pop | The sound made when hydrogen burns in air |
| Steam | Water in the gaseous state |

## Summary

- **Metal + Water → Metal hydroxide + Hydrogen**
- **Metal + Acid → Salt + Hydrogen**
- More reactive metals react more vigorously
- K, Na, Li react vigorously/dangerously with cold water
- Ca reacts steadily with cold water
- Mg, Zn, Fe react with steam but not cold water
- Cu, Ag, Au don't react with water or dilute acids
- Test for hydrogen: **squeaky pop** with burning splint
